trial_court: Family Court, Anand (Family Suit No. 164 of 2022)
case_name: Mehaben W/O Krushnakant Naranbhai ... vs Krishnakant Naranbhai Patel

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Mehaben W/O Krushnakant Naranbhai Patel, wife and mother
parties.respondent_defendant: Krishnakant Naranbhai Patel, husband and father

facts_of_case: Petitioner got married to respondent in 2013, had a son, but was tortured and harassed by respondent and his family. Petitioner returned to India after being deported from UK. Respondent filed for divorce at Family Court, Anand, while petitioner sought protection and filed a criminal application under Domestic Violence Act.

legal_principles.principle: A court may transfer a case to another court if the convenience of the parties is at stake.
legal_principles.held: Pressing into service judgment in the case of Tejalben v/ s. Mihirbhai Bharatbhai Kothari [AIR 2016 SC 718], it is sought to be submitted by learned advocate for the petitioner that the petitioner is lady living in Vadodara along her mother at parental home.
cited_cases: Tejalben v/ s. Mihirbhai Bharatbhai Kothari [AIR 2016 SC 718]

legal_principles.principle: A court may consider the inconvenience faced by a party in deciding whether to transfer a case.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, he would submit that the petitioner is urging to transfer Family Suit only on the ground of inconvenience she is facing.

use_for_drafting: drafting a transfer petition under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure
preparing a case for family court transfer
advising on grounds for transferring a family suit
